subject: Renewal: renegotiate tier for burst pocket and PO
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@cartology.com>, Priya Singh <priya@cartology.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation — proposal for tier adjustment + burst pocket

Hi Alex / Priya,

Happy Friday — quick note on Cartology's upcoming renewal (Apr 30). Based on the trailing three months of usage (seen some bursty traffic during nightly batch jobs + holiday promotion), we recommend a small step-up to the Hosted API committed tier to avoid throttles and preserve latency SLAs.

Proposal highlights (attached):
- Move from 1.5M to 2.25M committed tokens / month (interim 50% uplift)
- Add a dedicated burst pocket (200k tokens / month) that will apply before soft-throttle kicks in
- Preserve current per-token unit price for the base commit; burst units billed at standard overage rate but capped monthly

Attachments: Redwood_Hosted_Upsell_Proposal_Mar2028.pdf

Next steps I suggest: 1) confirm you want the uplift, 2) I'll route procurement worksheet to Karthik, 3) DocuSign for the SOW amendment and we target a May 1 start.

If you'd like a 20-min sync to walk the numbers with Karthik and Marissa, I can schedule for next week.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: Redwood_Hosted_Upsell_Proposal_Mar2028.pdf (proposal summary, pricing table, timeline)

Thanks Logan — appreciate the proactive read. A couple quick questions before we loop procurement:

1) Can you confirm unit pricing for the uplifted commit vs current? I see "preserve unit price" in the summary but want a line-item so procurement can sign off.
2) What SLA changes (if any) come with the burst pocket? Will the latency SLO be maintained for real-time endpoints?
3) Any discounts for annual prepay vs monthly billing?

Also, procurement at Cartology will want the worksheet pre-filled with our billing contact and PO language. If you can kick that over to Karthik now, we can move faster.

Alex

Hi team — filled in the worksheet and attached the redlines. Quick notes:
- Base unit price preserved for the uplift (2.25M) at $0.0009/token (same as current commit price).
- Burst pocket is an isolated bucket billed at $0.0015/token but capped at $300/month.
- Annual prepay (12 months) qualifies for a 7% discount on committed spend.
- No SLA changes: latency SLO for real-time endpoints remains at p95 < 120ms; burst pocket only affects soft-throttle thresholds, not routing.

I've attached: SOW_Amendment_Cartology.docx (ready for signature) and the completed Procurement_Worksheet_Cartology.xlsx.

Thanks Karthik — this looks good.

We reviewed internally; procurement has the worksheet and expects to issue a PO next week referencing the SOW amendment. We'll sign the DocuSign envelope once PO is in place (standard for us). Confirming the plan:
- Effective date: May 1, 2028
- Commit: 2.25M tokens/month base, 200k burst pocket (cap $300/month)
- Billing: annual prepay (we'll take the 7% discount)

Please send an onboarding checklist / ops contact for the May 1 handover. Also want a one-hour kickoff to review caching best practices and prefix caching so we don't hit unnecessary burst usage.

Alex Rivera
Head of Engineering, Cartology
